manuscripts.title: Effect of Financial Planning on Quality Service Delivery in  Telecommunication Companies in Rwanda
manuscripts.abstract:
This study investigated the contribution of financial planning on quality service delivery in 
telecommunication companies in Rwanda. The target population of this study is 103 respondents 
participated in this study. Structured, validated and reliable questionnaire was used. Based on 
the findings, results of the multiple regression showed that the adjusted R2
is 0.730 representing 
73.0% indicating that the financial planning components contribute to the quality service delivery. 
From ANOVA Table, the F-test is 70.093 has a p-value = 0.000. This implies that all financial 
planning components variables jointly have positive and significant effect on quality service 
delivery. Therefore, our null hypothesis which stated that there is no significant effect of financial 
planning components on quality service delivery in selected telecommunication companies in 
Rwanda is not accepted at all levels of significance. The study concluded that financial planning 
contributes positively to quality service delivery in telecommunication companies in Rwanda. It 
was recommended that during budgetary allocations, each department should be given a chance 
to participate in financial planning.

manuscripts.title: Contribution of Nurturing Learning Environment to Achieving Teaching  Objectives in Rwanda: Evidence from Selected Secondary Schools in Gasabo  District
manuscripts.abstract:
This study investigated the contribution of nurturing a learning environment to achieving teaching 
objectives in Rwanda. Through the descriptive research design, the researcher collected and 
analysed data from respondents. Regression research design was used because the researcher 
measured the relationship between the variables of the study. For this particular study, the 
population is 78 teachers of 6 selected public secondary schools in the Gasabo district. Those are 
14 teachers from GS Remera Catholic, 12 teachers from GS Kimironko I, 13 teachers from GS 
Musave, 11 teachers from GS Rugando, 13 teachers from GS Gisozi and 15 teachers from GS 
Kabuga. These schools were selected because they are Gasabo district public schools, which are 
fully funded by the government. To measure the relationship between Nurturing learning 
environment and achieving teaching objectives, regression analysis was used and the results 
indicated that the adjusted coefficient of determination was 0.948. This implies that the predictors 
of a nurturing learning environment affect the achievement of teaching objectives in secondary 
schools of the Gasabo district in Rwanda by 94.8%. In the end, schools in the Gasabo district are 
recommended to come up with strategies to increase students’ graduation rates since a large 
number of respondents disagreed that all of the enrolled students successfully finished their 
studies.

manuscripts.title: Contribution of Employee Motivation to Task Accomplishment in SMEs in  Rwanda: Evidence from Textile Industies (Dikam Fashion and New Kigali  Designers) in Kigali
manuscripts.abstract:
This study investigated the impact of employee motivation on task accomplishment in SMEs in 
Rwanda. A descriptive research approach was used, and questionnaires were distributed to 153 
respondents from DIKAM and New Kigali Designer. Regression analysis was adopted to 
statistically analyze the contribution of employee motivation on task accomplishment. The results 
indicated that the adjusted R2
is 0.231 representing 23.1%, indicating that the employee motivation 
components included in the model explains a relatively small portion of the variation in task 
accomplishment, while 0.769 representing 76.9% of task accomplishment is likely due to other 
factors that are not included in the model. According to the ANOVA Table, the F- test of 10.114 is
statistically significant with p < 0.05 indicated that the variables used in the model have a
goodness of fit and that are good predictors of task accomplishment. Therefore, H0 which states
that there is no significant effect of employee motivation components on task accomplishment is
rejected at all levels of significance. The study recommends prioritizing fair and competitive 
payment, fostering a positive working environments, and providing training to motivate 
employees. This can help address the operational challenges SMEs face, resulting in low 
performance and high failure rates.
